jobs.title: Strategic Finance Director
jobs.description:
ABOUT BEACON SOFTWARE

Beacon https://beaconsoftware.com/ is building the essential technology infrastructure for the everyday economy: the businesses, organizations, and services that make real life work, and that mainstream tech has largely left behind. We acquire, operate, and grow vertical market software companies. They are niche, founder-built businesses serving industries that are often overlooked and too profitable to ignore.

Our model is simple: we seek out founders who have built their business by spending years understanding their market and prioritizing their customers' specific needs. We buy great businesses, invest in their continued growth, and hold them permanently, accelerating that growth with an AI-native platform built specifically for vertical market software. No mandate to cut, flip, or roll up into something unrecognizable.

We are not a financial firm. We are technology entrepreneurs and operators who believe the most important businesses in the world are already running quietly in industries most people never think about. Our job is to find them, support the people who built them, and make them better.

Beacon is backed by a diverse base of investors, with $550M+ raised to date, including General Catalyst, Lightspeed, D1 Capital, CPMG, the family offices of the founders of Stripe, DoorDash, and Ramp, and evergreen funds built for the long game.




ROLE AND MISSION

This is an exciting and entrepreneurial opportunity to join a fast-paced technology company with a very significant growth trajectory. Beacon Software is making its first hire on the Strategic Finance team. This is a role where investing turns into building. The individual will report to Beacon’s VP, Strategic Finance and work closely with Beacon’s CEO, CTO, M&A Directors, industry pod leaders, and the General Managers of Beacon’s portfolio companies.



The Strategic Finance team’s mandate spans the financial decisions that shape Beacon: partnering with portfolio companies on growth and value creation, building AI-native systems that let functions scale non-linearly with the portfolio, owning Beacon’s capital allocation across organic and inorganic strategies, leading new strategy extensions beyond core software M&A, and building Beacon’s capital markets capability. Team members work across a mix of these areas based on their interests and skillset.



This is an asymmetric opportunity to build a company, with decision authority and velocity over process driving compounding equity. You’ll sit next to the CEO on capital allocation and capital markets, or fill a CFO role across dozens of companies on their most consequential decisions. The playbook will be shaped by you with the goal of building Beacon into a $100B company.



To succeed in this role, this individual should be an enthusiastic and energetic self-starter, with the ability to translate operator intuition into financial decisions and build the analytical rigor behind Beacon’s platform-level bets. The ability to manage multiple workstreams simultaneously across portfolio companies and platform initiatives will be essential. We are seeking a collaborative professional who wants to contribute ideas on how to improve the status quo and create best-practices that will accelerate our execution. Teamwork and positivity are key foundations of this growing team’s culture and ethos.



Location: for discussion. Beacon has offices in Toronto, San Francisco, New York, and Chicago.




WHAT YOU'LL DO

Finance partner to acquired companies

 - Partner with industry sector leaders and portfolio company General Managers as the financial decision-making engine across Beacon’s portfolio companies.

 - Translate product, AI, and operator intuition into investment decisions: pricing changes, sales hires, direct marketing investments, engineering allocation, and tuck-in M&A.

 - Build value creation plans, set budgets and targets, and make the day-to-day capital decisions that drive growth across companies.

Beacon capital allocation

 - Help own platform-level capital allocation: organic platform investment vs. inorganic M&A, platform-level acquisitions vs. tuck-ins, debt vs. equity at the corporate level.

 - Build the analytical rigor behind Beacon’s platform-level bets, ensuring capital is deployed where returns are most asymmetric.

Strategy extension beyond core software M&A

 - Own thesis through acquisition through ownership for new strategy extensions, starting with software-plus-services vertical integration in end markets where Beacon already owns software.

 - Partner with the M&A team for execution while driving the strategy, the diligence, and the post-close build.

Capital markets

 - Lead Beacon’s debt strategy, support future equity raises, and prepare Beacon for an eventual IPO.

 - Build best-in-class debt and equity investor relations and position Beacon as an institutional-grade capital allocator.

Build AI-native finance systems

 - Partner with Beacon’s CTO and engineering leadership on the company-wide tools that scale across the portfolio, including BeaconOS and AI-native financial systems.

 - Build the systems, dashboards, and decision frameworks that let sector leaders and GMs self-serve the financial answers they need, allowing the finance function to scale non-linearly with the portfolio.




QUALIFICATIONS

 - 3-8 years of post-undergrad experience in strategy consulting, private equity, or other finance roles (e.g., investment banking, growth equity, corporate development, or strategic finance).

 - Strong academic record from a competitive institution with a degree in Business, Finance, Economics, or a related quantitative field.

 - Investor mindset, analytical toolkit, and operator instinct: equally comfortable building a model and being in the room with a product leader or GM helping them make the call.

 - Expertise in building financial models, value creation plans, and analytical frameworks for capital allocation decisions.

 - Strong ability to synthesize complex systems and communicate clearly to senior stakeholders.

 - Familiarity with vertical market software, buy-and-build models, and the operating dynamics of small-to-mid-sized software businesses is a plus.

 - Excellent interpersonal and communication skills, with the ability to interact effectively with founders, CEOs, GMs, board members, and investors.

 - Ability to translate high-level objectives into actionable work plans and to manage multiple priorities simultaneously.

 - High attention to detail combined with the ability to zoom out and see the bigger picture.

 - Demonstrated high agency: comfort building the playbook, not just running it.

 - Curiosity and willingness to use AI tools heavily as part of the day-to-day workflow.

 - Conducts all interactions with a high level of integrity and trust.




WHAT YOU WILL GET FROM BEACON

 - A first-team seat on a small, high-leverage Strategic Finance group at the center of Beacon’s platform, with the opportunity to shape the playbook from day one.

 - Direct exposure to M&A, capital markets, AI-native systems, and IPO-grade operations.

 - Network and learn from leading public and private equity investors who are Beacon LPs, including the founders of Stripe, DoorDash, and Ramp.

 - Attend exclusive Beacon Speaker Series fireside chats with legendary venture capital, private equity, and hedge fund investors as well as eminent technology leaders.

 - Work directly with Silicon Valley product and engineering teams on portfolio value creation and platform technology investments.

 - Compounding equity in a company structured as a permanent capital vehicle, with no pressure to exit.

 - A clear line of sight from your work to enterprise value creation across dozens of operating companies.

 - A unique work environment that combines a high-growth technology startup with a long-term buy-and-hold investment platform.




IDEAL CANDIDATE

 - Based in or willing to work from Chicago. Location is for discussion for the right candidate.




POTENTIAL PERSONAS

 - Experience working at a top private equity, growth equity, or hedge fund.

 - Experience working at a top strategy consulting firm (MBB or equivalent).

 - Strategic finance or corporate development

 - Experience working at another serial acquirer, especially in software or vertical-market roll-ups.

 - Investment banking experience at a top-tier firm with software, technology, or M&A coverage.




MINIMUM EXPECTATIONS

 - Highly motivated with a strong work ethic.

 - Ability to manage multiple projects and deliverables simultaneously, with different timelines.




DESCRIPTORS OF PERSONAS THAT SUCCEED AT BEACON

 - High agency

 - Impatient with actions, patient with results

 - Play for front of the jersey

 - Intellectually curious

 - Perpetual learner

 - Low bureaucracy

 - Systems thinker

 - Optimistic

 - Commercial

 - Ambitious


Our Values at Beacon Software

 - Humility: We acknowledge that the path to getting to the right answer involves being wrong along the way. We have strong beliefs which are weakly held. We actively seek new ideas and believe we can learn from anyone at any time.

 - Honesty: We are truth seeking in our approach to business problems. Business is a repeat game and we believe that human relationships generate alpha. We understand that trust is earned over a lifetime and can be lost in an instant.

 - Hunger: We play to win. We hold ourselves to high standards and will not be outworked. We take pride in having a deep sense of responsibility to ourselves, each other, our partners, and our customers. We believe to whom much is given much is expected.

 - Horizon: We seek to build a generational software company. This will take decades. We manage our expectations and those of our partners to take advantage of the 8th wonder of the world - compounding growth.


How We Use AI in Our Hiring Process: To ensure transparency, we want candidates to know that Beacon Software uses Artificial Intelligence and AI-enabled tools to assist with screening, reviewing, organizing and highlighting profiles and applications that match the key requirements for each role.

 

AI does not make hiring decisions: Every application is reviewed by a member of our team, and all decisions throughout the process are made by humans. We use AI to support efficiency and consistency, not to replace human judgment. We are committed to a fair, thoughtful, and equitable experience for every candidate.

jobs.title: Recruiting Operations Lead
jobs.description:
ABOUT THE ROLE

Beacon's talent function is scaling fast, running in parallel across corporate functions and a growing roster of independently operated portfolio companies. Supporting each one of those searches are the systems and processes behind it: clean Ashby data, funnel and data reporting, and coordination that doesn't drop a candidate between steps. We're looking for a Recruiting Operations Lead to own that infrastructure end-to-end, and to build it right the first time, rather than retrofit in the future.




WHAT YOU'LL BE DOING

 - Own Ashby. Configuration, workflows, integrations, and data hygiene are yours end-to-end, not a shared responsibility with whoever has time.

 - Build the reporting layer. Funnel metrics, time-to-fill, source effectiveness, and hiring velocity, dashboards recruiters, executives, GMs, and hiring leadership use to make decisions.

 - Process design. Turn how Beacon hires today into documented, repeatable workflows that hold up as the team and portfolio grow.

 - Coordination backbone. Partner closely with our Recruiting Coordinator to keep scheduling, candidate communications, and interview logistics clean, especially with multiple portco searches running at once.

 - AI & automation. Identify and deploy tooling that reduces admin burden across candidate screening and scheduling. This might branch out to other areas including sourcing, and post interview decisions and offer workflows.

 - Candidate experience. Standardize the candidate journey across corporate and portco searches with a consistently high bar.

 - Cross-functional glue. Work with VP of Talent and Finance on headcount planning and with legal/People partners on offer letters, background checks, and clean handoffs.

 - Data hygiene at holdco scale. Every portfolio company's reqs, candidates, and hires need to roll up cleanly into one picture. You build that structure now, not after it's already messy.




WHAT YOU BRING

 - 5+ years in recruiting operations, HR technology, or business systems administration, with real ownership of an ATS (Ashby strongly preferred).

 - Comfort building process from scratch, not optimizing an existing one. Beacon's talent function is new; you'll be writing the manual, not editing it.

 - A strong analytical mindset. You can build a dashboard, but more importantly, you know which metric actually changes a decision.

 - Systems thinking. You can map how a change in one workflow ripples through downstream reporting and integrations before you make it.

 - Comfort with ambiguity in a fast-moving, small-team, multi-entity environment. No two portfolio companies operate the same way.

 - Excellent cross-functional communication; you'll work directly with the Talent, Department Heads/Managers, Finance, and People partners across a holding company structure.

 - Bachelor's degree, or additional years of experience in lieu.




BONUS POINTS

 - Experience in a PE-backed or multi-entity/holdco environment, where recruiting ops had to serve several operationally independent businesses at once.

 - Experience standing up recruiting ops and systems from scratch (0-to-1), not just optimizing a mature function.

 - Experience partnering with a lean recruiting coordination function to keep logistics tight without a large ops team behind you.


Our Values at Beacon Software

 - Humility: We acknowledge that the path to getting to the right answer involves being wrong along the way. We have strong beliefs which are weakly held. We actively seek new ideas and believe we can learn from anyone at any time.

 - Honesty: We are truth seeking in our approach to business problems. Business is a repeat game and we believe that human relationships generate alpha. We understand that trust is earned over a lifetime and can be lost in an instant.

 - Hunger: We play to win. We hold ourselves to high standards and will not be outworked. We take pride in having a deep sense of responsibility to ourselves, each other, our partners, and our customers. We believe to whom much is given much is expected.

 - Horizon: We seek to build a generational software company. This will take decades. We manage our expectations and those of our partners to take advantage of the 8th wonder of the world - compounding growth.

jobs.title: Chief of Staff, Office of CTO
jobs.description:
ABOUT BEACON:

Beacon is unlike most product companies. Where others start with a single core product and expand into adjacencies over time, portfolio diversity is a Day 0 reality for the organization. Every product and team across the portfolio operates differently.

The CTO’s internal "customers" range from portfolio company (portco) engineering teams and pod leaders to the deal team. Because of this multi-faceted structure, there is a constant stream of deeply technical, high-impact work that no single pod or portco owns. The complexity lies in the sheer heterogeneity: no two problems are the same, and they compound rapidly as new businesses are acquired and integrated.

Today, this work either lands directly on the CTO or does not happen. A technical Chief of Staff who can jump seamlessly in and out of unfamiliar codebases, architectures, and cross-functional teams closes that gap. The right candidate will increase overall leverage by an order of magnitude which is the baseline expectation for this role.




ABOUT THE ROLE:

 - On-the-Ground Execution: Work directly with the CTO and embed with portcos during critical inflection points. First priority: Solid Starts as they onboard Cortex and Arc. You will serve as the eyes, ears, and hands on the ground to ensure critical launches and migrations land smoothly.

 - Portfolio-Wide AI Leverage: Scale modern AI workflows (agentic coding, support deflection, inline AI features) across 30+ small, lean engineering teams that lack the bandwidth to figure it out independently. Help evaluate which portfolio products are durable vs. exposed to AI disruption.

 - End-to-End Tech M&A Diligence: Own the technical workstream post-LOI. Run tech overview sessions, audit target architectures, review codebases, analyze infrastructure costs, and write the technical debt POV for Deal Previews and the Investment Committee (IC). Crucially, you won't just write reports, you will carry diligence findings post-close to ensure remediation actually happens.

 - Cross-Functional & External Glue: Act as the connective tissue between engineering and deal, ops, finance, and pod leaders so technology never feels like a black box. Externally, serve as a face for Beacon in the San Francisco tech and founder scene through technical blog posts, architectural deep dives, and meetup talks to drive deal and talent top-of-funnel.

 - Technical Firefighting & Operations: Parachute into stalled migrations, outages, unexpected departures, or vendor renegotiations. Keep the CTO's operating cadence tight: prep and follow-through for pod tech reviews, IC materials, key tech KPIs (uptime, infra costs, velocity), and senior hiring loops.




WHAT YOU’LL DO:

Beacon is looking for a high-slope, high-agency individual who views this role as an elite apprenticeship—a chance to look inside 60+ software businesses from the ground floor before starting or running their next major venture.




WHAT BEACON IS LOOKING FOR:

 - Background: Ideally a former founder (3–4 years out of school, YC or equivalent accelerator background preferred). Must have experience working as a Chief of Staff at the Office of the CTO.

 - AI-Native Builder: Builds with agents and modern AI-assisted tools by default, not as an afterthought.

 - Hands-On & Versatile: Proven track record of building and shipping full-stack products end-to-end. Comfortable diving into unfamiliar stacks and reading code quickly.

 - Communication: Exceptional written and verbal communication skills; capable of writing technical blogs and communicating complex systems to non-technical stakeholders.

 - Mindset: Extreme hustle, high adaptability, and strong systems thinking. (Note: This is an elite technical execution role, not a project management or administrative EA position.)

jobs.title: HR Business Partner
jobs.description:
Beacon https://beaconsoftware.com is building the essential technology infrastructure for the everyday economy: the businesses, organizations, and services that make real life work, and that mainstream tech has largely left behind. We acquire, operate, and grow vertical market software companies — niche, founder-built businesses serving industries that are often overlooked and too profitable to ignore.

Our model is simple: we seek out founders who have built their business by spending years understanding their market and prioritizing their customers' specific needs. We buy great businesses, invest in their continued growth, and hold them permanently — accelerating that growth with an AI-native platform built specifically for vertical market software. No mandate to cut, flip, or roll up into something unrecognizable.

We are not a financial firm. We are technology entrepreneurs and operators who believe the most important businesses in the world are already running quietly in industries most people never think about. Our job is to find them, support the people who built them, and make them better.

Beacon is backed by a diverse base of investors, with $550M+ raised to date, including General Catalyst, Lightspeed, D1 Capital, CPMG, the family offices of the founders of Stripe, DoorDash, and Ramp, and evergreen funds built for the long game.




ABOUT THE ROLE

This is an exciting and entrepreneurial opportunity to join a fast-paced technology company with a very significant growth trajectory. Beacon Software is looking for an experienced HR Business Partner, with a background working for a high growth technology company. This individual will manage and oversee the HR function, at Beacon and across our acquired companies. This role is suited for an entrepreneurial individual with a strong HR and people’s operations background. The role involves building and subsequently optimizing processes, working across companies, and building/improving the company’s existing HR processes. The individual will report to Beacon's VP Business Operations and will work closely with the company's COO & CPO as well as the Group CPO’s across the different industry pods where Beacon owns companies.

To succeed in this role, this individual should be an enthusiastic and energetic self-starter with strong attention to detail. The ability to multitask and manage multiple projects at the same time will be an important asset. We are seeking a collaborative professional who likes to put forward suggestions and ideas on how to improve the status quo and create best-practices. Teamwork and positivity are key foundations of this growing finance group’s culture and ethos. As Beacon continues to grow, there is significant opportunity for growth, both individually and for the HR department.




RESPONSIBILITIES

 - Build and drive annual or multi-year people, org, and talent strategies tied to business goals.

 - Advise leaders on talent planning, retention, leadership capability, and change management.

 - Coach managers and leaders on performance management, feedback, development planning, employee engagement, and leading through change.

 - Own or support employee relations matters, including performance issues, conflict resolution, and sensitive employee concerns.

 - Run or improve core people programs such as onboarding, performance cycles, review processes, manager calibrations, compensation planning, engagement surveys, and career frameworks.

 - Oversee and improve end-to-end People Operations across the workforce lifecycle, from candidate and hiring operations through onboarding and offboarding.

 - Own workforce data integrity and operational controls, including documentation, auditability, and readiness for compliance or SOX-relevant requirements.

 - Oversee People systems and vendors, including ATS, HRIS, onboarding, payroll, and benefits tools, ensuring reliability and strong handoffs.

 - Bachelor’s or Master’s degree preferred, especially in an HR-related field, or equivalent experience.

 - Strong business acumen and the ability to translate business strategy into people, org, and talent decisions.

 - Proven experience partnering with senior leaders, executives, founders, or C-suite stakeholders on complex organizational and people topics. Working across multiple offices / geographies is a plus.

 - Strong analytical and data orientation, including interpreting people data, identifying trends or risks, and using insights to influence decisions.

 - Experience designing or improving org structures, talent strategies, and workforce planning to support scale, speed, and reduced friction.

 - Experience leading organizational change and building change leadership capability in others.

 - Strong relationship-building and influence skills across HR, cross-functional partners, leadership teams, managers, and employees.

 - Excellent judgment, emotional intelligence, tact, calm under pressure, and the ability to navigate sensitive situations with trust and empathy.

 - Ability to thrive in fast-paced, ambiguous, high-growth environments and adapt as priorities shift.

 - Builder/operator mindset: able to create scalable structure, processes, and systems while staying pragmatic and flexible.

 - Experience coaching leadership teams and managers, including performance, feedback, career development, and leadership effectiveness.

 - Strong written, verbal, and interpersonal communication skills, including comfort working with async and global teams.

jobs.title: Director - Governance, Risk, Compliance & Privacy (GRC)
jobs.description:
ABOUT BEACON SOFTWARE

Beacon https://beaconsoftware.com/ is acquiring and operating a portfolio of vertical SaaS companies. Most private equity firms scale by adding people. We are building Beacon to scale by adding software. The thesis is simple: portfolio operations, value creation, and deal sourcing are bottlenecked by human attention, and an agentic operating system can lift that ceiling by an order of magnitude.

We are looking for a GRC leader to build and scale the governance, risk, compliance, and privacy function for a growing portfolio of software companies. This is a founding, high-ownership role for someone who has built before and treats automation and modern AI tooling as the default way to operate.

Beacon has raised $550M+ from investors including General Catalyst, Lightspeed, D1 Capital, CPMG, and the family offices of the founders of Stripe, DoorDash, and Ramp.


 


ABOUT THE ROLE

Our GRC function is at an early, formative stage. You would shape it from the foundations and scale it across the portfolio, working directly with our portfolio companies to take them through their own audits and certifications, and designing a program that grows with the business rather than one built for a single audit. The mandate spans security compliance, data privacy, risk, and AI governance. We expect it to be built AI-first: modern automation platforms and LLM-assisted workflows over manual process.




WHAT YOU'LL DO

The role spans two scopes:

 - Beacon. The holdco's enterprise governance program: security policy, AI governance, data governance and privacy, enterprise and third-party risk, and posture reporting. Governance-led, including any frameworks Beacon itself elects to pursue.

 - Portfolio companies. Taking our portfolio companies through their own audits and certifications (SOC 2, ISO 27001, accessibility conformance, and others as their customers require), delivered hands-on as a repeatable service that scales across the portfolio.

Underpinning both: a common control architecture that maps a control once to satisfy many standards, AI-first automation, and clear program reporting.




WHO YOU ARE

 - You have built or substantially matured a GRC program before and taken an organization through SOC 2 Type 2. Typically several years (5+) in GRC, IT governance, or security compliance, though what you have built matters more to us than the count.

 - A builder with a bias for action. When you see a manual process, your first instinct is how to automate it.

 - A strong systems thinker. You design scalable GRC architectures, not one-off fixes for the next audit.

 - Fluent with a compliance automation platform (Vanta, Drata, Secureframe, or similar) and current on AI tooling in practice, not just in theory.

 - Comfortable across both security compliance and data privacy, or able to ramp quickly on regimes you have not personally run.

 - An excellent cross-functional communicator who works through influence and can translate compliance requirements into terms both technical and non-technical teams can act on.

 - A clear writer.

 - Worked in a fast paced, start-up environment.




BONUS POINTS

 - Privacy or audit certifications (CIPP, CIPM, CISA, CISSP, or ISO 27001 Lead Auditor or Implementer).

 - Experience with regimes beyond SOC 2 (ISO 27001, PCI DSS, HIPAA, FedRAMP, StateRAMP) and accessibility conformance (WCAG, VPAT).

 - Enough technical fluency to scope what the program needs and partner closely with engineering, even without building the tooling yourself.

 - Multi-entity, private-equity, or holding-company experience.

 - M&A security and privacy diligence experience.

jobs.title: Business Development Manager - Humanitarian Software
jobs.description:
About Humanitarian Software:

For 40 years, Humanitarian Software has designed and delivered supply chain solutions for humanitarian aid organizations, nonprofits, and NGOs. Our flagship platform, HELM, covers the full operational picture; gift-in-kind processing, donor restrictions, advanced warehousing, barcoding, DSCSA compliance, international shipping, last-mile delivery, analytics, and donor reporting. It replaces the spreadsheets and disconnected systems most relief organizations still run on with a single operational record, one that follows a donated pallet from the receiving dock to the field and proves to donors and regulators exactly where it went. Today HELM supports leading non-profit organizations and helps in the distribution of over $5 billion in aid worldwide each year.



Role Overview:

We are seeking a driven, organized, and commercially minded Business Development Manager to drive Humanitarian Software’s new business growth. The primary focus of this position is building a strong pipeline of qualified prospects by developing lead generation strategies, initiating new prospect relationships, and closing net-new logos.

You'll own the cycle end to end, from the top of the funnel through to closed-won: generating your pipeline, running discovery and demos in collaboration with sales engineers, and closing net-new customers in the humanitarian aid and disaster relief nonprofit space. Reporting to the GM, your work will contribute to scaling Humanitarian’s go-to market function, it is a builder’s seat with the autonomy to own the playbook and room to grow as the team expands.

This is a true full-cycle sales role. You will build and develop your own pipeline, work inbound and referral opportunities, lead qualification and discovery, coordinate solution demonstrations, manage the proposal and procurement process, and close net-new customers.

Responsibilities & Duties:

 - Pipeline generation: Build the ICP target list against the target segments, run outbound sales motion, work inbound and referral-sourced leads

 - Qualification: Score prospective customers against ICP, run budget/authority/timing checks, manage a long cycle without letting dead deals sit

 - Discovery & demo: Lead discovery conversation to understand their mission, workflows, and potential fit; brief the sales engineers that are running the demo

 - Proposal & close: Keep the deal moving through demo, solution design, and proposal. Work alongside the business operations team to navigate procurement cycles and close deals

 - Handoff: Clean transition to delivery at closed-won, staying involved as relationship owner through onboarding

Qualifications:

 - Experience and track record – 5–8 years in B2B software sales, with at least 3 years owning deals end to end and personally carrying a quota

 - Complex, consultative selling – experience selling into multi-stakeholder organizations; deals where finance, operations, and leadership all have a say, and procurement is part of the process

 - Pipeline generation – a track record of building your own pipeline through outbound prospecting, rather than working marketing or SDR generated leads

 - Communication and presence – strong communicator, comfortable initiating cold conversations and equally credible with a warehouse operations manager or an executive director; able to represent the company at industry events, conferences, and trade shows

 - Organized and methodical – the discipline to manage multiple long-running opportunities and keep CRM and pipeline data clean

 - Self-directed – comfortable building structure where none exists; this is a founding commercial seat, and the playbook does not exist yet

Nice to have:

 - Experience selling ERP, supply chain, warehouse mgmt., or other system-of-record software

 - Background in the humanitarian, NGO, non-profit, or international development sector

 - HubSpot or comparable CRM experience

 - Based in the Upstate SC area

 - Multilingual (Spanish, German, French)

What You’ll Get:

 - A profitable, growing business with real market position

 - An environment to learn and grow in your career

 - The opportunity to lead and shape the next phase of growth for Humanitarian Software
